title: Present Tense Verb Groups (1st, 2nd, and 3rd Conjugations)
subtitle: Conjugate verbs in the present tense by recognizing their stem vowel.
keyPoint: Bulgarian verbs are divided into three conjugations based on the 3rd person singular vowel: First (-е-), Second (-и-), and Third (-а-/-я-).

useCases.label: Habitual actions
useCases.example: Всяка сутрин пия кафе.

useCases.label: Current state
useCases.example: Сега живея в София.

useCases.label: Universal facts
useCases.example: Земята обикаля около слънцето.

examples.en: Аз чета интересна книга.
Ние говорим български език.
Те обичат хубава музика.
Ти пишеш писмо на приятел.
Вие работите ли днес?

mistakes.note: Third conjugation verbs add -м for the 1st person singular 'аз', not just the bare stem.
First and second conjugation 1st person plural takes -ем or -им, never -еме in standard written Bulgarian.
The 3rd person plural for the 2nd conjugation requires the ending -ят, not the singular form.

quiz.question: How do you say 'I speak' in Bulgarian?
quiz.explanation: 'Говоря' is the 1st person singular form for the 2nd-conjugation verb 'говоря'.

quiz.question: Complete: 'Ние ___ в София.' (We live in Sofia - живея)
quiz.explanation: The 1st conjugation 1st person plural ('ние') ending is -ем: 'живеем'.

quiz.question: Complete: 'Те ___ музика.' (They listen to music - слушам)
quiz.explanation: The 3rd conjugation 3rd person plural ('те') ending is -ат: 'слушат'.

quiz.question: Complete: 'Ти ___ ли български?' (Do you understand Bulgarian? - разбирам)
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person singular ('ти') ending for 3rd conjugation is -аш: 'разбираш'.

tip: To determine a verb's conjugation, look at its 'той/тя' (he/she) form: -е indicates 1st, -и indicates 2nd, and -а/-я indicates 3rd.

title: The Postposed Definite Article for Nouns
subtitle: Attach definite articles directly to the end of Bulgarian nouns.
keyPoint: Bulgarian lacks a standalone word for 'the'; instead, gender- and number-specific article endings are attached directly to the end of nouns.

useCases.label: Specific known object
useCases.example: Книгата е на масата.

useCases.label: Subject of the sentence
useCases.example: Мъжът чете вестник.

useCases.label: Direct object
useCases.example: Виждам града отдалеч.

examples.en: Градът е много стар.
Жената работи в училище.
Момчето играе в парка.
Книгите са на рафта.
Виждам мъжа на улицата.

mistakes.note: Use the definite article when referring to a specific book both speakers know about.
Use the full article (-ът / -ят) when a masculine noun is the grammatical subject of the sentence.
Feminine nouns take -та as their definite suffix, not just a consonant.

quiz.question: Complete: '___ е хубаво.' (The child is good - дете)
quiz.explanation: Neuter nouns take the definite suffix -то: 'детето'.

quiz.question: Which form is used for masculine subject: '___ е висок.' (The student is tall - студент)
quiz.explanation: Masculine nouns functioning as the grammatical subject take the full article ending -ът: 'студентът'.

quiz.question: Complete: '___ пие чай.' (The woman is drinking tea - жена)
quiz.explanation: Feminine singular nouns take the suffix -та: 'жената'.

quiz.question: Complete: '___ са нови.' (The tables are new - маси)
quiz.explanation: Plural nouns ending in -и take the definite suffix -те: 'масите'.

tip: Remember the 'rule of thumb' for masculine nouns: if you can replace it with 'той' (he), use the full article -ът/-ят; if with 'него' (him), use the short article -а/-я.

title: Vocative Case Endings
subtitle: Address people and things directly using vocative noun forms.
keyPoint: While Bulgarian has lost most case endings, it retains a distinct vocative form used exclusively for direct address.

useCases.label: Direct personal greeting
useCases.example: Здравей, Петре!

useCases.label: Calling someone over
useCases.example: Иване, ела тук!

useCases.label: Polite address to title
useCases.example: Господине, заповядайте!

examples.en: Добър ден, господине!
Здравей, Иване!
Ела бързо, сине!
Благодаря ти, приятелю!
Къде си, мамо?

mistakes.note: When addressing a gentleman directly, 'господин' takes the vocative ending -е.
Traditional masculine names ending in a consonant take -е when calling someone.
Do not mix the vocative (мамо) for direct calling with the nominative (мама) when talking about the person.

quiz.question: How do you address your mother directly? '___, къде си?'
quiz.explanation: The vocative form of 'мама' is 'мамо'.

quiz.question: Call your friend 'Петър' directly: 'Здравей, ___!'
quiz.explanation: Masculine 'Петър' drops the fleeting ъ and adds -е to become 'Петре'.

quiz.question: Address a friend directly: 'Здравей, ___!' (приятел)
quiz.explanation: Masculine nouns ending in soft consonants like -тел take the vocative suffix -ю: 'приятелю'.

quiz.question: Call a teacher politely: '___, имам въпрос.' (господин)
quiz.explanation: 'Господин' takes the vocative suffix -е: 'господине'.

tip: Many modern female personal names (like Анна, Елена) can colloquially remain without a vocative change to sound gentler, but traditional family terms like 'мамо' and 'бабо' always use -о.

title: Regular and Count Plural Forms of Nouns
subtitle: Form standard plurals and the special masculine count form after numbers.
keyPoint: Masculine non-person nouns must use the special count form (бройна форма) in -а/-я after numerals, while other nouns and people use the regular plural.

useCases.label: Count form after cardinal numbers
useCases.example: Имам два компютъра.

useCases.label: Regular plural without quantity
useCases.example: Тези градове са големи.

useCases.label: Counting male persons
useCases.example: В стаята има трима лекари.

examples.en: Купих два нови стола.
Всички столове са заети.
В офиса работят трима инженери.
Трябват ми пет лева.
На масата има четири ябълки.

mistakes.note: Non-person masculine nouns take the count form ending in -а/-я after numerals, not the regular plural.
Masculine nouns referring to human beings take the standard plural (-и), never the count form.
Do not attach the definite article to nouns immediately after indefinite numerals unless specifically specifying 'the three books'.

quiz.question: Complete: 'В града има пет ___.' (hotels - хотел)
quiz.explanation: Inanimate masculine noun 'хотел' uses the count form -а after numerals: 'пет хотела'.

quiz.question: Complete: 'В залата влязоха двама ___.' (professors - професор)
quiz.explanation: Human masculine nouns use the regular plural (-и) even after numerals: 'двама професори'.

quiz.question: Complete: 'Тези ___ са много удобни.' (chairs - стол)
quiz.explanation: Without a specific numeral, general plurality for 'стол' uses the regular plural 'столове'.

quiz.question: Complete: 'Това струва десет ___.' (levs - лев)
quiz.explanation: The currency unit 'лев' is a masculine inanimate noun and takes the count form ending -а after numbers: 'десет лева'.

tip: Use the count form (-а/-я) for masculine things and objects after numbers and 'колко' (how many), but stick to standard plurals for people!

title: Short Form Dative and Accusative Pronouns
subtitle: Master direct and indirect object clitics in everyday conversation.
keyPoint: Bulgarian uses short, unstressed clitic pronouns for direct (ме, те, го, я, ни, ви, ги) and indirect (ми, ти, му, ѝ, ни, ви, им) objects, placing them directly before the finite verb.

useCases.label: Direct object pronoun
useCases.example: Познавам го много добре.

useCases.label: Indirect object pronoun
useCases.example: Той ми дава книга.

useCases.label: Double object combination
useCases.example: Тя ми го дава.

examples.en: Аз те обичам.
Той ми каза истината.
Виждам я всеки ден.
Учителят ни помага.
Купих им подарък за празника.

mistakes.note: A short clitic pronoun cannot stand at the very beginning of a sentence; place it after the verb if no word precedes it.
When both short clitics are used, indirect (му) always precedes direct (го): indirect + direct.
The indirect feminine pronoun 'to her' is spelled with a grave accent (ѝ) to distinguish it from the conjunction 'и' (and).

quiz.question: Complete: 'Аз ___ виждам на спирката.' (I see him - direct object)
quiz.explanation: 'Го' is the accusative (direct object) clitic for 3rd person singular masculine 'him'.

quiz.question: Complete: 'Тя ___ даде книгата.' (She gave me the book - indirect object)
quiz.explanation: 'Ми' is the dative (indirect object) clitic for 1st person singular 'to me'.

quiz.question: Complete: 'Ние ___ обичаме много.' (We love you [informal sg.] - direct object)
quiz.explanation: 'Те' is the direct object clitic for 2nd person singular 'you'.

quiz.question: Complete: 'Майка ___ чете приказка.' (Mother reads them a story - indirect object)
quiz.explanation: 'Им' is the 3rd person plural indirect object pronoun meaning 'to them'.

tip: Never start a Bulgarian sentence with a clitic pronoun! If nothing comes before the verb, place the clitic immediately after the verb (e.g., 'Давам ти' instead of 'Ти давам').

title: Basic 'Da'-Constructions replacing the Infinitive
subtitle: Connecting conjugated verbs without an infinitive form
keyPoint: Bulgarian lacks an infinitive verb form, so it connects verbs using the particle 'да' followed by a fully conjugated present-tense verb matching the subject.

useCases.label: Desire and Intent (искам)
useCases.example: Искам да пия кафе.

useCases.label: Ability and Possibility (мога)
useCases.example: Мога да говоря български.

useCases.label: Obligation and Necessity (трябва)
useCases.example: Трябва да тръгваме сега.

examples.en: Искам да спя.
Той иска да яде ябълка.
Ние можем да помогнем.
Вие трябва да работите днес.
Децата не обичат да спят следобед.

mistakes.note: You cannot omit the conjunction 'да' between the two verbs.
The verb after 'да' must conjugate to agree with the subject (we = учим, not учи).
Never use a verbal noun after 'да'; use the conjugated finite verb form.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for 'I want to drink water': 'Искам ___ вода.'
quiz.explanation: 'Да' is required, followed by the first-person singular conjugated verb 'пия'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for 'We can come': 'Ние можем ___.'
quiz.explanation: The second verb must agree with 'ние' (1st person plural), yielding 'да дойдем'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for 'You (singular) must study': 'Трябва ___.'
quiz.explanation: Modal 'трябва' remains impersonal while the verb after 'да' conjugates for 'ти': 'да учиш'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for 'They love to travel': 'Те обичат ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'Те' requires the 3rd person plural ending '-ат', making 'да пътуват' correct.

tip: Think of 'да + conjugated verb' as Bulgarian's equivalent to the English infinitive 'to + verb'.

title: Full vs. Short Masculine Definite Article (Пълен и кратък член)
subtitle: Choosing between -ът/-ят and -а/-я for masculine singular nouns
keyPoint: Use the full article (-ът/-ят) when the masculine noun is the grammatical subject, and the short article (-а/-я) for direct objects, indirect objects, or after prepositions.

useCases.label: Subject Position
useCases.example: Влакът пристига на гарата.

useCases.label: Direct Object Position
useCases.example: Виждам влака отдалеч.

useCases.label: After Prepositions
useCases.example: Качвам се на влака.

examples.en: Мъжът чете интересна книга.
Познавам мъжа от вчера.
Учителят влезе в класната стая.
Дадох тетрадката на учителя.
Градът е много стар и красив.

mistakes.note: The subject performing the action must take the full article (-ът).
A noun acting as a direct object must take the short article (-а).
Nouns after prepositions always take the short article (-а/-я).

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for 'The student is reading': '___ чете нова книга.'
quiz.explanation: 'The student' is the subject of the sentence, so the full article '-ът' is required.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for 'I bought the computer': 'Купих ___ вчера.'
quiz.explanation: 'The computer' is the direct object of the verb 'купих', requiring the short article '-а'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for 'We are talking about the film': 'Говорим за ___.'
quiz.explanation: Any noun following a preposition (like 'за') takes the short article '-а'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for 'The teacher answered the question': '___ отговори на въпроса.'
quiz.explanation: 'Учител' is a soft-stem masculine noun acting as the subject, taking the full soft article '-ят'.

tip: Substitute the pronoun 'той' (he) or 'него' (him): if 'той' sounds right, use the full article (-ът/-ят); if 'него' fits, use the short article (-а/-я).

title: Clitic Doubling for Topicalization and Emphasis
subtitle: Pairing full noun phrases with matching short object pronouns
keyPoint: Bulgarian reinforces topicalized or fronted direct and indirect objects by pairing the full noun or pronoun with its corresponding short clitic pronoun.

useCases.label: Emphasizing Direct Objects
useCases.example: Тази книга я прочетох за един ден.

useCases.label: Fronted Indirect Recipients
useCases.example: На баща ми му купихме часовник.

useCases.label: Expressing Feelings / States
useCases.example: На мене ми е студено.

examples.en: Него го познавам много добре.
Книгата я оставих на масата.
На Петър му казаха истината.
На мене ми харесва тази музика.
Нея я търси директорът.

mistakes.note: The indirect clitic must match the feminine recipient (на Мария -> ѝ, not го).
'Книга' is feminine singular, so the doubling clitic must be direct feminine 'я'.

mistakes.right: На мене ми харесва този град.
mistakes.note: Impersonal sensory expressions like 'харесва' require the indirect dative frame ('на мене ми').

quiz.question: Fill the blank with the doubled direct clitic: 'Филма ___ гледах снощи.'
quiz.explanation: 'Филм' is masculine singular, so its direct object clitic is 'го'.

quiz.question: Fill the blank with the doubled indirect clitic: 'На сестра ми ___ подарих книга.'
quiz.explanation: 'На сестра ми' is feminine indirect (to her), requiring the short indirect dative clitic 'ѝ'.

quiz.question: Choose the missing pronoun: 'На децата ___ дадоха сладолед.'
quiz.explanation: 'На децата' is plural indirect (to them), requiring 'им'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct doubling pair: '___ ме поканиха на вечеря.'
quiz.explanation: The clitic 'ме' (1st person singular direct) pairs with the full direct pronoun 'мене'.

tip: Whenever you bring an object to the absolute beginning of a sentence to make it the topic, always echo it with a short clitic right before the verb.

title: Pronominal Clitic Placement and Wackernagel's Law
subtitle: Ordering clitics and preventing them from starting sentences
keyPoint: Bulgarian clitics cannot stand at the very beginning of a sentence; they lean on the verb or preceding words in the fixed order: Indirect Clitic + Direct Clitic + Verb.

cells: When the verb starts the sentence
When another word begins the sentence

useCases.label: Initial Verb Sentence
useCases.example: Обади ми се утре сутрин.

useCases.label: Non-Initial Preverbal Clitic
useCases.example: Вчера ми го донесоха.

useCases.label: Negated Verbal Phrase
useCases.example: Не му я давай днес.

examples.en: Казвам ти го за последен път.
Той ми я показа вчера.
Не му го казвай още.
Дай ми го, моля те!
Сега ви ги връщам.

mistakes.note: A clitic can never be the first word in a sentence; place it after the initial verb.
Indirect clitics (ми, ти, му, ѝ...) must strictly precede direct clitics (ме, те, го, я...).
The negative particle 'не' attracts clitics before the verb; do not put them after.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly begins with the verb?
quiz.explanation: Clitics cannot open a sentence; 'Дай ми книгата!' correctly places the clitic after the verb.

quiz.question: Select the correct clitic order for 'He is giving it to her': 'Той ___ дава.'
quiz.explanation: Indirect clitics precede direct clitics: 'ѝ' (to her) comes before 'го' (it/him).

quiz.question: How do you correctly negate 'Той ми го каза'?
quiz.explanation: The particle 'не' precedes the clitics, which in turn precede the verb: 'Той не ми го каза'.

quiz.question: Choose the grammatically sound sentence meaning 'I see you':
quiz.explanation: Because 'виждам' is the first word, the enclitic 'те' must follow: 'Виждам те'.

tip: Memorize the strict cluster formula: Indirect Clitic (to whom) + Direct Clitic (what) + Verb, unless the verb is the sentence's very first word.

title: Future Tense Formation with 'Ще' and Negation with 'Няма да'
subtitle: Expressing upcoming events in positive and negative sentences
keyPoint: Form the affirmative future tense using the invariant particle 'ще' before the present verb, and the negative future using the fixed construction 'няма да' plus the present verb.

useCases.label: Scheduled Events
useCases.example: Влакът ще замине в пет часа.

useCases.label: Promises and Plans
useCases.example: Ще ти помогна с домашната работа.

useCases.label: Refusals and Denials
useCases.example: Няма да отидем на кино довечера.

examples.en: Утре ще чета тази книга.
Ние ще дойдем навреме.
Той няма да работи в понеделник.
Аз няма да закъснея.
Ще вали ли дъжд следобед?

mistakes.note: Standard modern Bulgarian uses 'няма да' for future negation, not 'не ще'.
'Ще' never conjugates, but the main verb must agree with 'те' (3rd person plural: пътуват).
Do not mix 'ще' into negative sentences formed with 'няма да'.

quiz.question: Fill the blank for 'We will speak with the doctor': 'Ние ___ с лекаря.'
quiz.explanation: 'Ще' is placed before the 1st person plural present verb form 'говорим'.

quiz.question: Fill the blank for 'I will not come tomorrow': 'Утре ___ на срещата.'
quiz.explanation: The standard negative future construction is 'няма да' followed by the conjugated verb 'дойда'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase: '___ ли кафе утре сутрин?' (Will you drink...?)
quiz.explanation: 'Ще' pairs directly with the second-person singular verb 'пиеш'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly says 'They will not buy the house'?
quiz.explanation: 'Няма' is impersonal and never conjugates to 'нямат'; 'Те няма да купят къщата' is correct.

tip: 'Ще' is completely invariable and never changes for person or number; only conjugate the verb that immediately follows it!

title: Verbal Aspect: Imperfective vs. Perfective
subtitle: Mastering the fundamental division of Bulgarian verb stems
keyPoint: Imperfective verbs express ongoing, repeated, or general actions, whereas perfective verbs denote completed, single actions with a clear boundary or result.

useCases.label: Habitual or Ongoing Action
useCases.example: Всяка сутрин пия кафе и чета вестник.

useCases.label: One-Time Completed Result
useCases.example: Ще прочета тази интересна книга до утре.

useCases.label: Sequence of Completed Events
useCases.example: Той влезе в стаята и отвори прозореца.

examples.en: Всеки ден уча нови български думи.
Утре ще науча всички тези правила.
Обикновено пиша писма бавно.
Трябва да напиша имейл на шефа.
Той дълго чете статията, но накрая я разбра.

mistakes.wrong: Искам да прочитам тази книга сега.
mistakes.right: Искам да прочета тази книга сега.
mistakes.note: When expressing a desire to finish a specific single act, use the perfective stem with 'да'.

mistakes.wrong: Всяка вечер той прочете по една приказка.
mistakes.right: Всяка вечер той чете по една приказка.
mistakes.note: Habitual or repeated actions require imperfective aspect, not perfective.
Perfective verbs cannot stand alone as independent present tense predicates expressing regular habits.

quiz.question: Every day I ___ tea with lemon in the morning.
quiz.explanation: Regular repeated daily habits require the imperfective aspect (пия).

quiz.question: I have to ___ this letter right now.
quiz.explanation: A specific completed outcome in the immediate context takes the perfective form (да напиша).

quiz.question: Maria always ___ the windows on Saturdays.
quiz.explanation: The adverb 'винаги' (always) indicates repetition, demanding the imperfective present (отваря).

quiz.question: Tomorrow we will ___ a new car.
quiz.explanation: Future single events aiming at completion require the perfective stem after 'ще' (ще купим).

tip: Never use a standalone perfective verb in the present tense; it usually requires auxiliary particles like 'ще' (future) or 'да' (subjunctive).

title: Enclitic Possessive Pronouns and Kinship Terms
subtitle: Short dative clitics for natural, everyday possession
keyPoint: Short possessive clitics directly follow definite nouns with an article, but follow singular kinship terms without any article.

useCases.label: Singular Kinship
useCases.example: Майка ми готви много вкусно.

useCases.label: Possession with Definite Nouns
useCases.example: Колата му е паркирана отпред.

useCases.label: Body Parts and Personal Objects
useCases.example: Главата ме боли, очите ми са уморени.

examples.en: Баща ми работи в голяма болница.
Къде живее брат ти сега?
Новият апартамент на сестра ѝ е просторен.
Парите ми са в чантата.
Кучето ни обича дългите разходки в парка.

mistakes.note: Singular kinship terms take possessive clitics directly, without the definite article suffix.
Standard non-kinship nouns must take the definite article when paired with a possessive clitic.
Use 'ѝ' with a grave accent for the feminine possessive clitic 'her', not the conjunction 'и' (and).

quiz.question: How do you say 'my brother'?
quiz.explanation: Singular kinship words like 'брат' take clitics directly without a definite article: 'брат ми'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase: 'our house'.
quiz.explanation: Regular nouns take the definite article before appending the enclitic: 'къщата ни'.

quiz.question: Her sister is very smart: '___ е много умна.'
quiz.explanation: Kinship words take no article and 'her' requires the accented pronoun 'ѝ'.

quiz.question: Where is your car? -> Къде е ___?
quiz.explanation: 'Кола' is not a kinship term, so it must be definite: 'колата ти'.

tip: In Bulgarian, adjectives pull the definite article! If an adjective precedes the noun, the clitic attaches to that adjective: 'моята стара майка' or 'добрата ми приятелка'.

title: The Aorist Tense (Минало свършено време)
subtitle: Conjugating verbs to narrate completed past actions
keyPoint: The aorist tense expresses an action completed at a specific point in the past, formed using specific theme vowels and the endings -х, -хме, -хте, -ха.

useCases.label: Sequential Past Events
useCases.example: Той влезе, поздрави и седна на стола.

useCases.label: Action with Stated Completion
useCases.example: Снощи изгледахме целия филм.

useCases.label: Sudden Past Occurrence
useCases.example: Изведнъж токът спря и телефонът звънна.

examples.en: Вчера написах дълго писмо до приятел.
Тя прочете статията за десет минути.
Миналата седмица купихме нов диван.
Те чуха силния шум на улицата.
Защо не ми каза истината тогава?

mistakes.note: Use the past aorist tense rather than the present tense for completed events in the past.
The second person singular ('ти') ending does not have '-х'; it drops the ending or takes the bare stem.
Watch out for false definite article usage in Bulgarian when nouns are introduced generally in the past.

quiz.question: Yesterday we ___ the whole book. (прочета)
quiz.explanation: The 1st person plural ('ние') aorist ending is '-хме': 'прочетохме'.

quiz.question: She ___ home late last night. (се прибера)
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person singular aorist of 'прибера се' drops the -х marker to yield 'се прибра'.

quiz.question: They ___ what happened. (разбера)
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person plural ('те') aorist ending is '-ха': 'разбраха'.

quiz.question: Did you (sing.) ___ that noise? (чуя)
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person singular ('ти') of 'чуя' in the aorist is simply 'чу'.

tip: Notice that in the aorist, the 2nd person ('ти') and 3rd person singular ('той/тя/то') forms look completely identical (e.g., ти написа, той написа).

title: The Imperfect Tense (Минало несвършено време)
subtitle: Conjugating verbs for ongoing background and past habits
keyPoint: The imperfect tense depicts an action in progress, background context, or a repeating habit viewed from a past vantage point, using suffixes with -ше- or -я-.

useCases.label: Past Action in Progress
useCases.example: Докато четях книгата, някой почука на вратата.

useCases.label: Simultaneous Background Scenery
useCases.example: Слънцето грееше и птиците пееха весело.

useCases.label: Past Habitual Routine
useCases.example: Като малък играех навън по цял ден.

examples.en: Докато тя спеше, навън валеше дъжд.
Когато бяхме деца, всяко лято прекарвахме на село.
Той често мислеше за родния си град.
Ние говорехме за политика цяла нощ.
Те живееха в Пловдив преди десет години.

mistakes.wrong: Докато аз прочетох книгата, той влезе.
mistakes.right: Докато аз четях книгата, той влезе.
mistakes.note: Background ongoing processes framing another action require the imperfect tense (четях), not the aorist.
The 2nd and 3rd person singular imperfect ending is '-ше', without '-х'.

mistakes.wrong: Вчера валеше дъжд за пет минути и спря.
mistakes.right: Вчера валя дъжд за пет минути и спря.
mistakes.note: If the total duration is delimited as a single complete past event, Bulgarian prefers the aorist (валя).

quiz.question: While we ___ dinner, the phone rang. (готвя)
quiz.explanation: An ongoing background activity interrupted by another past action uses the imperfect ('готвехме').

quiz.question: When I was young, I ___ football every Sunday. (играя)
quiz.explanation: Past recurring habits from a continuous perspective take the imperfect: 'аз играех'.

quiz.question: The sun ___ brightly all afternoon. (грея)
quiz.explanation: Atmospheric past background descriptions typically take the 3rd person imperfect: 'грееше'.

quiz.question: What were they ___ at that moment? (правя)
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person plural ('те') imperfect form of 'правя' is 'правеха'.

tip: The distinctive fingerprint of the imperfect is the ending '-ше' in both the 2nd (ти) and 3rd person (той/тя) singular, unlike the aorist which drops this suffix.

title: Aspectual Interaction: Aorist vs. Imperfect
subtitle: Unlocking the 2x2 matrix of Bulgarian past tenses and aspects
keyPoint: Bulgarian combines two aspects with two past tenses, allowing both imperfective aorists (durative blocks) and perfective imperfects (habitual repeated completed actions).

cells: Action viewed as a closed durative event
Hypothetical or repeated completed act (e.g. с 'щом')

useCases.label: Imperfective Aorist (Closed Duration)
useCases.example: Вчера четох два часа и после излязох.

useCases.label: Perfective Imperfect (Past Iteration)
useCases.example: Щом решеше задачата, веднага започваше нова.

useCases.label: Interrupted Line (Impf. Impf + Perf. Aorist)
useCases.example: Докато вървях към парка, срещнах Иван.

examples.en: Снощи спах осем часа.
Когато чуеше гласа ѝ, той се усмихваше.
Цял ден учих за трудния изпит.
Винаги щом видеше куче, тя се плашеше.
Вчера говорих с майка ми по телефона.

mistakes.note: Use imperfective imperfect (спяхме) for ongoing background, and perfective aorist (звънна) for the interruption.

mistakes.wrong: Всеки път щом той напише писмото, го пращаше.
mistakes.right: Всеки път щом той напишеше писмото, го пращаше.
mistakes.note: In past repeated sequences, the perfective verb requires the imperfect past ending (напишеше), not present tense.
Duration expressions ('цял следобед') focus on the process over time, calling for the imperfective aorist (четох).

quiz.question: Yesterday I worked for three hours: 'Вчера ___ три часа.'
quiz.explanation: 'Работих' is an imperfective aorist: an uncompleted-type verb packaged as a closed past block of time.

quiz.question: Whenever he ___ a word, he looked it up. (сбъркам - perf. imperfect)
quiz.explanation: The perfective imperfect 'сбъркаше' denotes a repeated, complete action whenever triggered in the past.

quiz.question: While she ___ dinner, Peter arrived. (imperfect + aorist)
quiz.explanation: The background process uses imperfective imperfect ('готвеше') and the interrupting event uses perfective aorist ('пристигна').

quiz.question: The perfective imperfect form of 'прочета' (3rd person sing.) is:
quiz.explanation: 'Прочете' is perfective aorist, while 'прочетеше' is the perfective imperfect form used in subordinate iterative clauses.

tip: Think of the Imperfective Aorist ('четох') as answering 'Did you spend time doing it?' without caring whether you finished, whereas the Perfective Aorist ('прочетох') means 'Did you finish it?'.

title: Past Indefinite and Past Perfect
subtitle: Master compound past tenses using the 'l'-participle with present and imperfect forms of 'съм'
keyPoint: The Past Indefinite pairs the present tense of 'съм' with the past active participle to denote relevance to now, while the Past Perfect pairs the imperfect of 'съм' with the participle for prior past actions.

cells: Аз бях чел преди да дойдеш.

useCases.label: Life Experience (Indefinite)
useCases.example: Никога не съм пътувал до Япония.

useCases.label: Past Result Relevant Now
useCases.example: Той е загубил ключовете си и не може да влезе.

useCases.label: Action Prior to Past Point
useCases.example: Когато пристигнахме, влакът вече беше заминал.

examples.en: Ние сме посетили много красиви градове в Европа.
Тя е написала прекрасно писмо до родителите си.
Преди да се обадиш, аз вече бях приготвил вечерята.
Те бяха завършили проекта преди крайния срок.
Вие чели ли сте този роман на Вазов?

mistakes.note: The auxiliary 'е' cannot be omitted in standard Past Indefinite, and the participle must agree in gender with the feminine subject.
The participle must agree in number (plural ending '-ли') with plural subjects like 'ние'.

mistakes.wrong: Когато дойде, аз съм тръгнал вече.
mistakes.right: Когато дойде, аз вече бях тръгнал.
mistakes.note: Use the Past Perfect ('бях тръгнал') instead of Past Indefinite for actions completed before another past event.

quiz.question: Maria ___ to Sofia several times.
quiz.explanation: 'Мария' is 3rd person singular feminine, requiring 'е' plus the feminine participle 'пътувала'.

quiz.question: When Ivan arrived, we ___ the movie.
quiz.explanation: An action completed before another past moment takes the Past Perfect ('бяхме изгледали' for 'ние').

quiz.question: Have you (plural) ever ___ this traditional dish?
quiz.explanation: Questions in the Past Indefinite place 'ли' after the participle or auxiliary: 'опитвали ли сте'.

quiz.question: Peter ___ his homework before his mother returned home.
quiz.explanation: Third person singular Past Perfect requires 'беше' + masculine participle 'написал'.

tip: Never omit the 3rd person auxiliary 'е' or 'са' in the Past Indefinite; dropping them accidentally turns your sentence into the Renarrative mood!

title: Articulated Relative Pronouns
subtitle: Connect subordinate clauses accurately using 'който', 'която', 'което', and 'които'
keyPoint: Bulgarian relative pronouns agree in gender and number with the antecedent noun and take the definite article form (-то), with masculine accusative using 'когото'.

useCases.label: Subject of Subordinate Clause
useCases.example: Това е писателят, който спечели наградата.

useCases.label: Direct Object of Subordinate Clause
useCases.example: Лекарят, когото търсите, е в кабинета.

useCases.label: Prepositional Object Reference
useCases.example: Къщата, в която живеем, е много стара.

examples.en: Момичето, което седи до прозореца, чете интересна книга.
Това са приятелите, с които пътувахме до морето.
Учителят, на когото благодарихме, беше много развълнуван.
Търся книгата, която ми препоръча вчера.
Мъжът, който говори по телефона, е моят директор.

mistakes.note: Relative pronouns must be articulated (-то) and masculine human direct objects require 'когото'.

mistakes.wrong: Жената, който живее тук, е лекарка.
mistakes.right: Жената, която живее тук, е лекарка.
mistakes.note: The pronoun must agree in gender with the feminine antecedent 'жената'.
Always maintain the plural marker '-ито' for plural referents, preceded by prepositions when necessary.

quiz.question: The building in ___ they work is located downtown.
quiz.explanation: 'Сграда' (implied: сградата) is feminine singular, so it requires 'в която'.

quiz.question: The students ___ passed the exam are celebrating.
quiz.explanation: 'Студентите' is plural, requiring the plural relative pronoun 'които'.

quiz.question: The man ___ we saw at the station is an engineer.
quiz.explanation: A masculine singular person functioning as direct object takes the special accusative form 'когото'.

quiz.question: The village in ___ my grandparents live is peaceful.
quiz.explanation: 'Село' is neuter singular, requiring 'в което'.

tip: For masculine human antecedents, ask whether the pronoun is the subject ('който') or object ('когото/на когото') inside the clause.

title: The Renarrative Mood
subtitle: Report indirect, hearsay, or unwitnessed statements accurately in Bulgarian
keyPoint: The Renarrative mood conveys hearsay or unwitnessed events by using 'l'-participles while crucially dropping the 3rd person auxiliaries 'е' and 'са'.

useCases.label: Hearsay / Second-hand News
useCases.example: Казват, че министърът подал оставка вчера.

useCases.label: Unwitnessed Past Events
useCases.example: Преди векове тук живял могъщ владетел.

useCases.label: Doubt or Distancing
useCases.example: Той твърди, че нямал време за срещата.

examples.en: Според вестниците инцидентът станал късно снощи.
Тя каза, че Мария заминала за Лондон миналата седмица.
Разправят, че новите съседи купили скъпа кола.
Иван не дойде, защото бил болен от грип.
Когато полицията пристигнала, крадците вече били избягали.

mistakes.wrong: Казват, че той е заминал вчера.
mistakes.note: Retaining 'е' marks the sentence as an eyewitness/factual Past Indefinite rather than reported speech.

mistakes.wrong: Те казаха, че са били там.
mistakes.note: In 3rd person plural renarrative, omit the auxiliary 'са'.

mistakes.wrong: Тя разбрала, че той е имал проблем.
mistakes.right: Тя разбрала, че той имал проблем.
mistakes.note: Both verbs in renarrated context drop the 3rd person auxiliary to maintain modal consistency.

quiz.question: Reported: 'They say that Peter bought a new apartment.'
quiz.explanation: In 3rd person singular renarrative, the auxiliary 'е' is omitted: 'купил'.

quiz.question: Reported: 'According to rumors, the witnesses ___ afraid to speak.'
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person plural renarrative drops 'са', leaving only the participle 'били'.

quiz.question: Reported: 'Elena claimed she ___ late because the bus broke down.'
quiz.explanation: Renarrative of an unwitnessed result drops 'е', using the feminine participle 'закъсняла'.

quiz.question: Which sentence contains an eyewitness statement, NOT a renarrative?
quiz.explanation: 'Иван е написал' retains 'е', indicating eyewitness Past Indefinite rather than reported speech.

tip: The fastest diagnostic test: if 'е' or 'са' is present with the 'l'-participle in 3rd person, it is indicative; if dropped, it is renarrative.

title: Adverbial and Passive Past Participles
subtitle: Express simultaneous action with '-йки' and form passive constructions with '-н/-т'
keyPoint: Adverbial participles (-йки) express an action simultaneous to the main verb sharing the same subject, while passive past participles (-н/-т) inflect like adjectives to form passive states.

useCases.label: Simultaneous Manner/Action
useCases.example: Тя влезе в стаята, усмихвайки се топло.

useCases.label: Present State via Passive
useCases.example: Всички важни документи вече са подписани.

useCases.label: Past Passive Result
useCases.example: Мостът беше построен преди пет години.

examples.en: Четейки сутрешния вестник, баща ми пиеше кафе.
Сградата беше напълно разрушена от силното земетресение.
Слушайки любимата си песен, тя си спомни за дома.
Тази интересна статия е написана от известен журналист.
Всички билети за концерта са вече продадени.

mistakes.wrong: Вървейки по улицата, шапката му падна.
mistakes.right: Докато вървеше по улицата, шапката му падна.
mistakes.note: Dangling participle: the subject of the adverbial participle (-йки) MUST be identical to the main clause subject.
Passive past participles function as adjectives and must agree in gender with the subject ('книгата' is feminine).
The adverbial participle in '-йки' can only be formed from IMPERFECTIVE verbs, never perfective ones.

quiz.question: While ___ the coffee, she was talking on the phone.
quiz.explanation: Form the adverbial participle from the imperfective stem 'пия' -> 'пиейки'.

quiz.question: The newly built house was ___ last month.
quiz.explanation: 'Къщата' is feminine singular, so the passive participle must be 'продадена'.

quiz.question: The computers in the office are already ___.
quiz.explanation: 'Компютрите' is plural, requiring the plural passive participle ending '-ни' ('поправени').

quiz.question: Why is 'Направийки това, той си тръгна' incorrect?
options: Adverbial participles cannot be formed from perfective verbs like 'направя'.
quiz.explanation: Bulgarian adverbial participles in '-йки' can strictly be formed only from imperfective verbs (e.g., 'правейки', not 'направийки').

tip: Remember that '-йки' is completely invariable (it never takes gender/number endings), whereas passive participles in '-н/-т' inflect just like adjectives!

title: Conditional Mood with 'Бих'
subtitle: Construct polite requests and hypothetical conditional clauses using 'бих' and 'l'-participles
keyPoint: The Bulgarian conditional mood is formed using the special invariant past auxiliary stem 'бих-' inflected for person, followed by the active 'l'-participle.

useCases.label: Polite Requests & Wishes
useCases.example: Бих искал чаша минерална вода, моля.

useCases.label: Hypothetical Present/Future
useCases.example: Ако имахме пари, бихме си купили нова къща.

useCases.label: Unreal Past Hypotheses
useCases.example: Ако беше попитал, щяхме да ти помогнем.

examples.en: Аз бих желал да резервирам една двойна стая.
Ако времето беше хубаво, бихме отишли на планина.
Те биха приели предложението, ако условията бяха по-добри.
Ти би ли ми услужил с химикалка за минута?
Никой не би повярвал на такава невероятна история.

mistakes.wrong: Аз би искал да кажа нещо.
mistakes.right: Аз бих искал да кажа нещо.
mistakes.note: The 1st person singular auxiliary is 'бих', whereas 'би' is strictly for 2nd and 3rd person singular.
The 'l'-participle must agree in number with the subject: use plural 'отишли' with 'ние'.
When the conditional is followed by 'да', the subsequent verb inflects in the present personal form ('те да помогнат').

quiz.question: I would gladly ___ to you if I knew the answer.
quiz.explanation: First-person singular requires 'бих' alongside the masculine participle 'казал'.

quiz.question: They ___ buy that car if it were cheaper.
quiz.explanation: Third-person plural auxiliary is 'биха', combined with plural participle 'купили'.

quiz.question: Would you (informal singular) ___ to join us for dinner?
quiz.explanation: Second-person singular uses 'би' + masculine/feminine participle: 'би искал'.

quiz.question: We ___ happy to meet with the delegates tomorrow.
quiz.explanation: First-person plural requires 'бихме' + plural participle 'радвали'.

tip: Notice that 'би' serves for BOTH 2nd and 3rd person singular ('ти би казал', 'той би казал'), making it exceptionally easy to memorize!
